clue.text: Sundry charges on parts of the amusements

definitions.note: plural noun phrase: individual amusements such as side-shows

indicators.note: in a down or across charade, on means placed after, so the charges come after the sundry word

parts.note: divers is an old word for sundry or various
ions are electrically charged particles

explanation.surface: Various fees are added on to the cost of parts of a funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' reads like fees, but it means electrically charged particles.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is a pastime or entertainment, one of the things that amuse people.

clue.text: Learner gets in a spot, being a dunce

indicators.note: the learner gets in, so its letter goes inside the word for spot

parts.note: a dot is a small spot
L is the learner-driver plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: A learner who finds himself in a tight spot looks a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are synonyms for a stupid person.

clue.text: Six bringing skill to practicality

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
ability is a synonym for skill

explanation.surface: Six people bring their expertise to make a project workable.
explanation.definitionFit: Viability is the quality of being workable or practicable, a near synonym.

clue.text: Stretch of river?

parts.note: read both as a length of water between bends and, with the question mark, as the verb stretch meaning extend an arm

explanation.surface: A clue asking for a length of water along a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight length of a river is called by this name, and the word also means to stretch out.

clue.text: It's not right for in-law to embrace divorcee

indicators.note: the in-law pieces wrap around the divorcee, so one sits inside the other

parts.note: read as IN plus law, with an act being a law passed by parliament
an ex is a former spouse

explanation.surface: Someone protests that it is wrong for a relative by marriage to hug a former wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in-law' reads as a relative by marriage, but the hyphen splits it into a preposition and a word for law; 'to embrace' puts the former spouse between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means imprecise, so something not right or accurate.

clue.text: One sold out of soup ingredient

indicators.note: the letters of one sold come out of their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soup ingredient has sold out, with only one left.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles are strips of pasta often added to soups such as chicken noodle.

clue.text: Heroic record set by Olympic finalists

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
the final letters of Olympic, its last two, finishing the word

explanation.surface: A heroic record is set by the athletes who reach an Olympic final.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic describes something on a grand heroic scale, like an epic poem about heroes.

clue.text: A number after a new hip flask

indicators.note: the number is placed after the rearranged letters
new tells us the letters of a hip are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone gets a hip flask some time after a hip replacement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges A HIP into PHIA, and L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A phial is a small glass bottle, a kind of little flask.

clue.text: Remunerate ace postmen perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of ace postmen might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A suggestion that excellent postal workers should be paid more.
explanation.definitionFit: To compensate someone is to pay them for work or loss, the same as remunerate.

clue.text: Select a different reel for game fish

parts.note: to pick is to select

indicators.note: a different arrangement of the word reel is called for

explanation.surface: An angler chooses another reel to catch a sporting fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickerel is a small pike, a fish caught for sport.

clue.text: Lash out, take in a foreign capital

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take in the article, holding it inside
out signals that the letters of lash are scrambled

explanation.surface: An order to lash out and take in a city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LASH into LHSA, which takes in A after the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital city of Tibet, a foreign capital to the British setter.

clue.text: Amorous incitement to crime is wrong

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of to crime is are in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A moralist declares that sexual provocation leading to crime is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Eroticism is sexual arousal or desire, which an amorous incitement produces.

clue.text: Bouncer drunk at dance?

parts.note: high is slang for intoxicated
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman gets drunk at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' suggests a doorman; in cricket a bouncer is a ball pitched to rise high at the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bouncer is a short-pitched delivery that rears up as a high ball.

clue.text: A boomerang for Miss Minogue

definitions.meaning: in Western Australian Aboriginal usage a ... is a hunting boomerang
the first name of the Australian pop singer Minogue

explanation.surface: A boomerang named after an Australian pop star.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aboriginal word for a throwing stick is also the singer Minogue's first name.

clue.text: Sort of policy for the Lib. Dems?

definitions.text: Sort of policy for the Lib. Dems?

parts.words: Sort of policy for the Lib. Dems?
parts.note: an insurance policy covering others, punning on the Liberal Democrats as Britain's third-largest party

explanation.surface: A question about what political policy suits the Liberal Democrats.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-party insurance covers claims by others; the Liberal Democrats are traditionally Britain's third party after Labour and the Conservatives.

clue.text: Reduction in capital growth

parts.note: read as finance talk, but capital means the head and growth means hair

explanation.surface: An economist describes a slowdown in investment gains.
explanation.walkthrough: The financial reading is a decoy; the head's growth is trimmed at the barber's.
explanation.definitionFit: Trimming the hair reduces the growth on the head, and in finance a haircut is also a cut in an asset's value.

clue.text: Support excellent hero

definitions.meaning: to ... a cause is to support it
a winner or hero, and as an informal adjective it means excellent

explanation.surface: Backing for a splendid hero.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to back a cause; as a noun it means a winner or defender.

clue.text: Coastal navigators may pass through such difficulties

definitions.text: Coastal navigators may pass through such
definitions.meaning: narrow sea channels between land masses
being in dire ... means being in trouble

explanation.surface: Sailors near the shore may have to steer through tricky passages.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow channel of sea, and the plural also means a fix or predicament.

clue.text: Even the most generous would be deaf to such appeals

definitions.text: Even the most generous would be deaf to such appeals

parts.words: Even the most generous would be deaf to such appeals
parts.note: appeals for charity that nobody responds to, because they cannot be heard at all

explanation.surface: Some charity appeals fail to move even the kindest donors.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeals too quiet to be heard are unheard by anyone, however charitable.

clue.text: The personification of cunning

parts.note: the fox character of medieval European fables, the embodiment of craftiness

explanation.surface: A description of a sly character in literature.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the trickster fox in medieval beast fables, used for any fox.

clue.text: Trouble with fog in the vessel obtaining shark

indicators.note: the vessel obtains the scrambled letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a dish is a serving vessel

indicators.note: to trouble something is to disturb it, so the letters of fog are stirred up

explanation.surface: Fog causes trouble for a vessel catching a shark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' looks like the definition-free start of the surface, but it is the anagram signal on the word fog, and 'obtaining' has the dish hold the result.
explanation.definitionFit: The dogfish is a small shark common in British waters.

clue.text: Flirt and annoy worker

parts.note: to gall is to irritate or annoy
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A man who flirts both irritates and labours.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant is a ladies' man who pays court to women, so a flirt.

clue.text: Persevering and making progress

explanation.surface: Keeping at something and getting somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means continuing despite difficulty and also advancing or taking place.

clue.text: Built to accommodate people

definitions.meaning: past tense, a building that has been erected
to give guests a bed for the night

explanation.surface: A house was constructed to provide lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to erect a structure and to give someone lodging.

clue.text: Heady decoration for a woman

parts.note: heady is read literally, as worn on the head, rather than intoxicating

explanation.surface: An exciting adornment for a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled half-crown worn on the head by women on formal occasions.

clue.text: A downhill slide

parts.note: a controlled glide down a snow slope by a climber, or a gliding ballet step

explanation.surface: A description of decline, as of fortunes going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: In mountaineering, the word names a slide down a snowy slope on the feet.

clue.text: A name that might suit one

definitions.text: A name that might suit one

parts.words: A name that might suit one
parts.note: a man's first name, and also a twill cloth that might be made into a suit

explanation.surface: Someone muses on which name would suit a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name of French origin and a durable woollen fabric used for suits.

clue.text: The sign of the cross

parts.note: not the religious gesture but the cross-shaped symbol used in addition

explanation.surface: A reference to the religious gesture made by Christians.
explanation.definitionFit: The mathematical symbol for addition is an upright cross.

clue.text: Anger is no use for clear function of the brain

indicators.note: to use something is to work it over, so the letters of anger is no are reworked

explanation.surface: Anger is no good when the mind needs clarity.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning is logical thought, the brain's clear-headed faculty.

clue.text: A revolting subject

parts.note: revolting read as rising in revolt rather than disgusting, and subject as a citizen of a monarch

explanation.surface: A disgusting topic of conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject who rises in revolt against the crown is an insurgent.

clue.text: Right? Yes, first time

indicators.note: first tells us the word for yes comes before the right abbreviation

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes

explanation.surface: Someone checks that something is correct and gets a yes on the first try.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a period of time, twelve months long.

clue.text: Eternal state of one only having high notes?

definitions.text: state of one only having high notes
definitions.meaning: carrying only banknotes of large value, so no coins, no small money at all

explanation.surface: A singer who only hits top notes stays forever the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high notes' suggests singing, but means large banknotes: someone with no coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal never alters, and a person with only big banknotes has no coins.
